target_moa.text: Liraglutide is an acylated human GLP-1 receptor agonist with 97% amino acid sequence homology to endogenous human GLP-1(7-37); like GLP-1(7-37) it activates the GLP-1 receptor, enhancing glucose-dependent insulin secretion.

citations.quote: Liraglutide is an acylated human Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist with 97% amino acid sequence homology to endogenous human GLP-1(7-37).
GLP-1 is an intestinal peptide released in response to food ingestion that has an enhancing effect on insulin secretion when serum glucose is elevated and also has an inhibitory effect on glucagon

modality.text: peptide (acylated human GLP-1 analog produced by recombinant DNA)

citations.quote: Victoza contains liraglutide, an analog of human GLP-1 and acts as a GLP-1 receptor agonist. The peptide precursor of liraglutide, produced by a process that includes expression of recombinant DNA in *Saccharomyces cerevisiae*, has been engineered to be 97% homologous to native human GLP-1 by substituting arginine for lysine at position 34.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=5% and more common than placebo): headache, nausea, diarrhea, and anti-liraglutide antibody formation. In the 52-week monotherapy trial nausea occurred in 28.4% of Victoza vs 8.5% glimepiride, and diarrhea 17.1% vs 8.9%. Serious concerns include pancreatitis and serious hypoglycemia (when used with an insulin secretagogue).

detail.text: WARNING: RISK OF THYROID C-CELL TUMORS. Liraglutide causes dose-dependent and treatment-duration-dependent thyroid C-cell tumors at clinically relevant exposures in both genders of rats and mice; human relevance is unknown. Victoza is contraindicated in patients with a personal or family history of MTC or Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2).

citations.quote: Liraglutide causes dose-dependent and treatment-duration-dependent thyroid C-cell tumors at clinically relevant exposures in both genders of rats and mice. It is unknown whether Victoza causes thyroid C-cell tumors, including medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), in humans, as human relevance could not be ruled out by clinical or nonclinical studies. Victoza is contraindicated in patients with a personal or family history of MTC and in patients with Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2).

summary.text: Victoza (liraglutide) was approved under a traditional (full) approval as a 505(b) new drug application for glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus, based on a 52-week monotherapy trial and four 26-week add-on combination trials; approval was accompanied by a REMS (Medication Guide and communication plan) and numerous required postmarketing studies addressing thyroid C-cell tumor, pancreatitis, and cardiovascular risks. The application was reviewed by the Endocrinology and Metabolism Advisory Committee.

citations.quote: Please refer to your March 23, 2008, new drug application (NDA) submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Victoza (liraglutide [rDNA origin]) injection, solution for subcutaneous use.
The safety of Victoza was evaluated in a 52-week monotherapy trial and in four 26-week, add-on combination therapy trials.

Your proposed REMS, submitted on January 21, 2010, and appended to this letter, is approved. The REMS consists of a Medication Guide, a communication plan, and a timetable for submission of assessments of the REMS.
